Robot Doctor Mechanisms

Chain or belt skips or falls off

Clicking, slipping teeth, or the chain jumps off. Below are the 4 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 4 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Does the chain or belt feel loose or sag in the middle? Press the middle of the run with a finger.
  • Does the chain or belt wrap less than a quarter of any sprocket or pulley? Look at how much of each sprocket the chain actually touches.
  • If you draw a marker line across the hub and shaft, does it split after running? Draw one straight line over the hub (or collar) and the shaft, run it a few times, and look again.
  • With power off, does the mechanism move smoothly by hand through its whole range? Backdrive it slowly. Feel for tight spots, grinding, or places it catches.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 Chain or belt tension is wrong

Too loose and it skips teeth or falls off. Too tight and it strains the motor.

How to fix it 15 min

  1. Press the middle of the run. It should flex a little but not sag.
  2. Add an adjustable tensioner. Chain stretches over time, faster on small sprockets.
  3. Over-tightening burns out motors and wears bearings, so do not crank it.

Sources: GM0 · Chain · GM0 · Belt

2 Not enough wrap or bad alignment

Chain and belt need at least 90° of contact on each sprocket (180°+ is best) and must run straight.

How to fix it 20 min

  1. Count how much of each sprocket or pulley the chain or belt touches. Under 90° skips easily. Add an idler to wrap more.
  2. Lay a straight edge across both sprockets. Misalignment walks the chain off and breaks belts.
  3. Replace master links with a chain breaker joint where you can. Master links can pop off.

Sources: GM0 · Chain · GM0 · Belt

3 Hub or collar slipping on the shaft

Set screws work loose and chew the shaft, so the gear or sprocket spins while the shaft does not (or the reverse).

How to fix it 15 min

  1. Mark the shaft and hub with a marker line. If the lines separate after a run, it is slipping.
  2. Switch to clamping hubs and collars, or hex / D-shaft hubs, wherever possible.
  3. If you must use set screws, file a flat on round shafts and use blue threadlocker on metal (never on plastic).
  4. Use nylon locknuts everywhere. Plain nuts vibrate loose.

Sources: GM0 · Building tips · GM0 · Shaft retention

4 Mechanism is jammed or overloaded

If the mechanism binds or the load is too heavy for the gearing, the motor stalls. It hums, heats up, and drains the battery.

How to fix it 15 min

  1. Power off and move the mechanism by hand through its full range. It should move smoothly with no tight spots.
  2. Feel the motor after a run. Hot means it is stalling or working far too hard.
  3. Check for over-tightened chain or belt, misaligned shafts, screws hitting things, or a hard stop the code keeps pushing into.
  4. If the load really is too heavy, add reduction or a second motor. The RoboCodex gear ratio calculator helps size it.

Sources: GM0 · Building tips · FTC Docs · Power management
